operations.specification: User registration endpoint for creating new accounts. This operation allows users to create an account without any additional information beyond basic authentication data.
operations.description:
This endpoint handles user registration for the Todo application.

Users must provide authentication credentials to create a new account, after which the system issues an initial JWT token.

Authentication data is stored securely in the database with minimal required fields ensuring simplicity and speed.
The implementation follows the business requirement for a minimal registration process with no unnecessary fields or steps.

The system validates the input to ensure it meets basic security requirements before proceeding with account creation.
operations.summary: User registration endpoint, creates a new account with authentication data

requestBody.description: Registration request payload. Contains authentication credentials required to create a new account.

responseBody.description: Registration success response including token information.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: User login endpoint for authenticating existing accounts. This operation verifies user credentials and returns access tokens.
operations.description:
This endpoint authenticates existing users by validating their credentials and issuing access tokens.

Users must provide their authentication credentials to access the service. The system validates the provided credential against stored data to ensure a matching user account exists.

The endpoint implements security best practices for authentication, including secure token generation and protection against common authentication attacks.
The implementation strictly follows the minimal authentication requirements defined for this service, with no additional steps or confirmation screens required.
The business requirement for zero-friction user access is met through this streamlined login process.
operations.summary: User login endpoint, authenticates credentials and returns tokens

requestBody.description: Login request payload. Contains credentials for authentication.

responseBody.description: Login success response with authentication tokens.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Token refresh operation for extending active session duration. This allows users to renew their access token without re-authenticating.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows users to refresh their authentication tokens when the current access token is nearing expiration.

Users must provide a valid refresh token to extend their session duration. The system verifies the refresh token's validity and generates a new access token.
The endpoint supports automatic token renewal during active usage while maintaining session security.

The implementation follows the business requirement for a 15-minute session duration with automatic renewal, ensuring users remain authenticated without frequent login prompts.

The process is designed for minimal user interaction, providing a seamless experience consistent with the application's simplicity focus.
operations.summary: Token refresh endpoint, extends session duration without re-authentication

requestBody.description: Refresh token request payload. Contains the current refresh token to renew the session.

responseBody.description: Token refresh success response with new access token.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of todo items for the current user. The operation is designed to serve the primary user workflow of viewing their task list without complexity. The API automatically filters out any todo items marked as deleted (where deleted_at is set), respecting the soft delete mechanism defined in the Prisma schema. This ensures users only see active todos in their list, though the system retains deleted items for possible recovery. Data is ordered by creation date (newest first), providing a natural flow for users to see their most recent tasks at the top of the list. The response includes necessary pagination information for the frontend to handle large todo lists.
operations.description:
This operation retrieves a paginated list of todo items for the current user. The operation is designed to serve the primary user workflow of viewing their task list without complexity.

The API automatically filters out any todo items marked as deleted (where deleted_at is set), respecting the soft delete mechanism defined in the Prisma schema. This ensures users only see active todos in their list, though the system retains deleted items for possible recovery.

Data is ordered by creation date (newest first), providing a natural flow for users to see their most recent tasks at the top of the list. The response includes necessary pagination information for the frontend to handle large todo lists.

The operation supports a full suite of business rules regarding todo item display:
- Pending todos appear with normal styling
- Completed todos appear with a completion indication
- Only active todos (not marked as deleted) are returned
- The system respects the soft delete column to avoid data loss
operations.summary: Retrieve a paginated list of todo items (completed and pending)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo items including title, completion status, and timestamps

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation creates a new to-do item with a specified title. The new to-do item is created with completed status set to false and current timestamps for creation and update. It validates the title meets length requirements (1-100 characters) before saving to the database.
operations.description:
This operation creates a new to-do item with the provided title. The creation process enforces the following business rules:

- The title must be between 1 and 100 characters long
- The title must not contain invalid characters that could break data processing
- The new to-do item is automatically created with completed status set to false
- The creation timestamp (created_at) is set to the current time
- The update timestamp (updated_at) is also set to the current time

The system validates incoming title data for length and content before creating the new entry. Validation errors include "Title must be between 1-100 characters" and "Title must not be empty".

Upon successful creation, the new to-do item is returned with all standard properties including the auto-generated ID, title, completion status, and timestamps. The API does not allow creation of todos with the same title as existing todos within the same account.
operations.summary: Create a new to-do item with title

requestBody.description: The title of the to-do item to create

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a single todo item by its unique identifier (id). It is designed for the retrieval of a specific to-do item and is intended to be used when users need to view or edit a particular to-do item individually.
operations.description:
Retrieves a single todo item from the database by its unique ID. This operation supports both active and soft-deleted todos, but returns only non-deleted items to the user. If the item has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), it will not be returned in the response.

This operation is designed to provide a detailed view of a single to-do item, including its title, completion status, and timestamps. The response includes only the item's essential data required for display and editing purposes.

Security considerations include checking that the user has access to this specific item (though this is simplified to no authentication requirement for MVP). The operation properly handles soft deletion by excluding deleted items from the response, maintaining data integrity.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single todo item by ID

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo (UUID format)

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the requested todo item

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: Todo item must exist before it can be retrieved

operations.specification: This operation updates a todo item's title and/or completion status. It is designed for modifying specific to-do items by their primary identifier.
operations.description:
Updates the title or completion status of a specific todo item identified by its ID. This operation supports partial updates, allowing users to modify either the title (to rename a to-do item) or the completion status (to mark an item as completed or pending).

The operation validates the input data, ensuring title remains within 1-100 characters, and handles completion status changes appropriately. If the todo item has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), the operation will not allow modifications to that item.

Security considerations include ensuring the user is authorized to modify this item (authentication required). The operation correctly handles updates to the updated_at timestamp automatically, reducing the need for explicit client-side timestamp management. Business logic requires that the completion status can be toggled but that the title must maintain length validations.
operations.summary: Update a todo item (title or completion status)

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo (UUID format)

requestBody.description: Data to update for the todo item

responseBody.description: Updated information about the todo item

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: Todo item must exist before it can be updated

operations.specification: This operation deletes a todo item by marking it as deleted using a soft delete mechanism. It updates the deleted_at timestamp rather than permanently removing the record from the database, enabling potential recovery if needed.
operations.description:
This operation permanently removes the todo item from active views through a soft delete mechanism. The todo item is not physically removed from the database but has the 'deleted_at' timestamp set to the current time.

The soft delete approach allows for data recovery if needed while maintaining the historical tracking of all todo items. This implementation follows industry best practices for data integrity and business continuity.

When this API call is successful, the deleted todo item is no longer shown in standard todo listings and cannot be accessed except through system-administrative functions or historical records.

The todo item remains in the database with its original content (title, completed status) but with the 'deleted_at' timestamp set, indicating it's no longer active.
operations.summary: Delete a todo item with soft delete mechanism

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item to delete

responseBody.description: The todo item with its current state and deletion timestamp

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: Todo item must exist before it can be deleted

Schema definition for the to-do item entity, including all standard fields from the database.

#### Schema Definition

This schema represents the to-do item entity as it should be presented to the user.

#### Property Descriptions

---

#### Example Description Structure

This property represents the unique identifier for a to-do item.

The identifier is automatically generated by the system and is used to reference this to-do item in all API operations.

The UUID format used ensures global uniqueness and security, preventing predictable patterns in identifiers.

Example usage: "a7b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8".

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table (todo_todos) Column: id
- Prisma Comment: Primary Key.
- Constraints: Must be a valid UUID string.
- Business Constraint: Id must be globally unique across all to-do items.
- Validation: System validates UUID format prior to storage.

#### Value Examples

- "a7b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-g1h2-i3j4k5l6m7n8" (valid UUID)
- "xyz123" (invalid - not a standard UUID format)

#### Business Rule Context

The ID is the fundamental unique identifier for the to-do item throughout the application. It's used in all API endpoints (like /todos/{id}), as the primary way to reference specific to-do items across the system. The UUID format prevents any security vulnerabilities related to predictable incremental IDs and ensures reliable data integrity.

---

#### Example Description Structure

This property represents the text title of a to-do item, which is required for each to-do entry.

The title must be between 1 and 100 characters in length to ensure it's meaningful without being overly verbose.

Invalid titles include empty values or those exceeding the character limit. The title serves as the primary identifier for to-do items in the user interface.

Example usage: "Buy groceries", "Write report", "Schedule meeting".

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table (todo_todos) Column: title
- Prisma Comment: The to-do item title, required for each item.
- Constraints: min length 1, max length 100 characters.
- Business Constraint: Titles must be descriptive enough for users to identify the task quickly.
- Validation: Application enforces this length constraint during creation and update operations.

#### Value Examples

- "Buy groceries" (valid)
- "" (invalid - empty string)
- "Very long title that exceeds the 100 character limit and would cause display issues in user interface" (invalid - too long)

#### Business Rule Context

Titles are the most important user-facing property of the to-do item. They're used in the list view, search, and as quick identifiers during task management. The 1-100 character constraint balances usability with performance, ensuring titles fit within the layout constraints without truncation.

This field is required for all to-do item creation operations and must be validated before persisting to the database. The title is the fundamental input that drives the to-do functionality, making it essential to enforce clear business logic around its acceptance and usage.

---

#### Example Description Structure

This property indicates whether the to-do item has been completed (true) or not (false).

The completion status serves as the primary indicator of the to-do item's state in user interfaces.

It can be toggled by users via the UI to reflect their progress, affecting how the item appears in the list view.

Example usage: false (task not completed), true (task completed).

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table (todo_todos) Column: completed
- Prisma Comment: Whether the to-do item has been completed (true) or not (false).
- Constraints: Boolean value (true/false).
- Business Constraint: Completion state is the fundamental status of the to-do item.
- Validation: System ensures only valid boolean values are stored.

#### Value Examples

- true (valid - completed)
- false (valid - not completed)
- 1 (invalid - must be boolean)

#### Business Rule Context

The completion status is the core user interaction point for the to-do application. It directly matches the user's actions of checking tasks as complete. The UI provides a clear toggle control to update this status, which then triggers both the visual updates to the list and the backend update to this field.

This field has a strong business meaning as it represents the item's progress state. When this property changes from false to true, it triggers the task to move to the completed section in the UI, providing clear visual feedback to the user.

---

#### Example Description Structure

This property represents the timestamp when the to-do item was created, stored in UTC.

The creation timestamp provides a historical record of when the to-do item was added to the system.

All to-do items must have a valid creation timestamp to maintain accurate historical tracking and sorting.

Example usage: "2024-11-28T09:30:00.000Z".

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table (todo_todos) Column: created_at
- Prisma Comment: The timestamp when the to-do item was created.
- Constraints: ISO 8601 format, UTC.
- Business Constraint: Creation time is used for sorting and historical references.
- Validation: System validates proper ISO format during storage.

#### Value Examples

- "2024-11-28T09:30:00.000Z" (valid)
- "2024-11-28T09:30:00" (valid ISO date-time without milliseconds)
- "28/11/2024" (invalid - wrong format)

#### Business Rule Context

The creation timestamp establishes the chronology of to-do items, which is critical for sorting the list with most recent items at the top. This historical record is used for statistics and reporting. The timestamp is automatically set when a to-do item is created, and its values are used for the "created_at" field in the database.

This field is always present in to-do items and should not be modified during updates. It serves as the point of reference for tracking when a task was added to the list, which is essential for accurate time-based sorting and reporting.

---

#### Example Description Structure

This property represents the last update timestamp when the to-do item was modified, stored in UTC.

The last update timestamp indicates when the to-do item was last changed, whether by title updates or completion status changes.

This timestamp is automatically maintained by the system to provide accurate historical tracking of modifications.

Example usage: "2024-11-28T09:35:00.000Z".

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table (todo_todos) Column: updated_at
- Prisma Comment: The timestamp when the to-do item was last updated.
- Constraints: ISO 8601 format, UTC.
- Business Constraint: Updated time is used for sorting and tracking changes.
- Validation: System validates proper ISO format during storage.

#### Value Examples

- "2024-11-28T09:35:00.000Z" (valid)
- "2024-11-28T09:35" (valid ISO without milliseconds)
- "Nov 28 2024" (invalid - wrong format)

#### Business Rule Context

The updated timestamp is used for two main purposes: to indicate the most recent changes to to-do items and to provide a way to sort items by modification date. This timestamp is automatically updated whenever the to-do item's title or completion status changes, providing a clear record of the to-do item's history.

This field is always present in to-do items and is automatically managed by the system. It plays a role in user experience by ensuring that more recently updated items appear near the top of the list, reflecting the user's most recent activity.

---

#### Example Description Structure

This property represents the timestamp when the to-do item was soft-deleted, if it has been deleted.

The deletion timestamp allows for record-keeping of deleted to-do items without permanently removing them from the database.

This field is set to a specific timestamp when the item is soft-deleted, allowing for potential data recovery.

Example usage: "2024-11-28T10:00:00.000Z".

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table (todo_todos) Column: deleted_at
- Prisma Comment: The timestamp when the to-do item was deleted (soft delete).
- Constraints: ISO 8601 format, UTC, and can be null for active items.
- Business Constraint: Soft deletion allows for historical tracking and potential recovery.
- Validation: System validates proper ISO format when set.

#### Value Examples

- "2024-11-28T10:00:00.000Z" (valid soft delete timestamp)
- null (used for active items, no deletion)
- "2024-11-28" (invalid - requires full datetime)

#### Business Rule Context

The soft delete mechanism (using deleted_at) is a business decision to preserve historical data while removing items from active views. This approach enables potential data recovery if needed by the user or system, unlike hard deletion which permanently removes the record.

When this field is populated (not null), the to-do item is considered removed from active use. The timestamp is stored for audit purposes, allowing administrators to view when items were deleted. The system does not automatically restore items - they require manual recovery procedures, which aren't implemented in the MVP for this application.

ITodoTodo.IUpdate.description:
Type used for updating existing to-do items. It contains only the fields that can be modified by the user, including the task title and completion status.

Unlike the main entity type, the update type does not include any system-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) as these are not meant to be overridden by user input. This type is designed for partial updates (PATCH) where users may update only the title or completion status.

Key purpose: Allow modifications to a to-do item without requiring the user to include fields they don't want to change.

Business context: This type supports the MVP's goal of minimal user input by including only the relevant fields for updates. It follows the atomic operation principle by allowing a single API call to modify specific aspects of a to-do item.

Note: The update type uses the same naming convention as required by the system (with the dot for variant) and only includes fields that should be mutable by users.

#### Example Description Structure

This property represents the email address for user authentication.

The email address is used as the primary identifier for the user account.

Email validation follows standard format requirements to ensure validity and prevent invalid registrations.

Example usage: 'user@example.com', 'j.smith@company.com'.

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table (users) Column: email
- Prisma Comment: User's email address for authentication. Must be a valid email format.
- Constraints: Valid email format (e.g., 'user@domain.com').
- Business Constraint: Email is used as the primary authentication method for user accounts.
- Validation: System validates email format during registration and login.

#### Value Examples

- 'user@example.com' (valid)
- 'example' (invalid - missing '@' and domain)
- 'user@' (invalid - missing domain)
- '@example.com' (invalid - missing username)

#### Business Rule Context

The email field serves as the primary user identifier for authentication purposes. It's the first piece of information users provide when creating an account. The system enforces strict email validation rules to ensure all accounts use properly formatted identifiers, preventing invalid entries in the user database and simplifying account recovery processes.

---

#### Example Description Structure

This property represents the user's password for authentication.

The password is submitted in plain text during registration to be handled securely by the system.

The system handles all hashing and security processing to protect user credentials without requiring clients to manage any cryptographic operations.

Example usage: 'p@ssw0rd123', 'S3cur3P4ss!', 'aBcDeFgH'.

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table (users) Column: password
- Prisma Comment: User's password for authentication. This must be plain text for the registration process as the system will handle hashing.
- Constraints: Minimum of 1 character, maximum of 256 characters.
- Business Constraint: Passwords must be strong according to security policy standards.
- Validation: System validates password strength requirements and handles password hashing.

#### Value Examples

- 'p@ssw0rd123' (valid)
- 'password' (invalid - too weak)
- 'a' (invalid - too short)
- 'a123456789012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890' (invalid - too long)

#### Business Rule Context

The password field is a security-critical component of user authentication. The system never stores passwords in plaintext, instead using secure hashing algorithms. The user provides the password in plain text for registration, and the system handles all cryptographic operations. This separation of responsibility ensures that password management remains secure without placing additional complexity on client applications.

---

#### Example Description Structure

This property represents the client's IP address for session tracking.

The IP address is optional, as the server can often extract it from the request context.

Client may provide this value when using server-side rendering scenarios where the server doesn't have access to the request context.

Example usage: '192.168.1.1', '10.0.0.1'.

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table: Not applicable (client-provided session metadata)
- Constraints: Valid IPv4 format (e.g., '192.168.1.1'), optional.
- Business Constraint: Session tracking requires IP address for security monitoring.
- Validation: System validates IP format when provided.

#### Value Examples

- '192.168.1.1' (valid)
- '10.0.0.1' (valid)
- '10.0.0.1.5' (invalid - wrong format)

#### Business Rule Context

Session tracking includes capturing the client's IP address to help protect against unauthorized access and provide security context. While the server can often obtain this information from incoming requests, it's useful to include in the request payload for server-side rendering scenarios where the server might not have direct access to the client's network information. This field is optional and can be omitted if the server can infer the IP address.

---

#### Example Description Structure

This property represents the connection URL (current page URL) for session tracking.

The connection URL must be provided by the client to establish the session context.

This is mandatory because the server cannot infer the current page URL from the request data alone.

Example usage: 'https://app.example.com/signup', 'https://example.com/register'.

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table: Not applicable (client-provided session metadata)
- Constraints: Valid URI format, mandatory.
- Business Constraint: Session tracking requires reference to the current page URL.
- Validation: System validates URI format.

#### Value Examples

- 'https://app.example.com/signup' (valid)
- 'htp://wrong-protocol.com' (invalid - wrong protocol)
- '' (invalid - empty value)

#### Business Rule Context

The connection URL (href) is critical for session creation. It helps the application track which page the user is currently viewing when they create a session, which is useful for analytics, security monitoring, and user journey tracking. This field is mandatory because the server cannot know this information solely from the request, and the client must provide it to establish the session context correctly.

---

#### Example Description Structure

This property represents the referrer URL (previous page URL) for session tracking.

The referrer URL must be provided by the client to establish the session context.

This is mandatory because the server cannot infer the previous page URL from the request data alone.

Example usage: 'https://app.example.com/signin', 'https://example.com/login'.

#### Property Reference

- Prisma Table: Not applicable (client-provided session metadata)
- Constraints: Valid URI format, mandatory.
- Business Constraint: Session tracking requires reference to the previous page URL.
- Validation: System validates URI format.

#### Value Examples

- 'https://app.example.com/signin' (valid)
- 'http://example.com/login' (valid)
- '' (invalid - empty value)

#### Business Rule Context

The referrer URL helps the system understand the user's journey leading to the current page. This information is crucial for user experience analysis and site navigation improvement efforts. For security reasons, it's required to capture both the current page (href) and the previous page (referrer) to have a complete context for session management and security monitoring. This field is mandatory because the server cannot reliably determine the referrer from other parts of the request.


This interface is used for account registration, which is a self-signup operation requiring session context fields (ip, href, referrer) to establish proper session tracking and security monitoring.

ITodoTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a todo item for list views and references. Contains the minimal essential information needed to display a todo item in a list or as a reference in other entities.

- The `id` property provides a globally unique identifier for the todo item.
- The `title` property contains the user's brief description of the task.
- The `completed` property indicates whether the task has been finished, with true indicating completion and false indicating pending status.

This summary representation is optimized for performance in list views, providing only the essential information without any full-text details or timestamp metadata that would increase payload size and network overhead.

Note: System-managed fields like created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are intentionally excluded from summary representations to maintain the minimalistic design philosophy of the todo application. The summary type focuses solely on the business-relevant information that users need to see in a list context, leaving detailed information for full entity representations when explicitly requested.
